1.

The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as Act) by the investigating officer of FIR No.33/2019 Police Station Pandav Nagar, Delhi.
2.
The accident in the present case took place in the intervening night of 17/18.02.2019.
Rahul Jain and the petitioner Yash Kumar Gupta were going from Vikas Marg towards Mangal Bazar side on their scooter registration No. DL-7SCG-7972.
Rahul Jain was driving this scooter and Yash Kumar Gupta was sitting as pillion.

When they reached near Solitare Hotel, Vikas Marg, a car (Honda City)
registration No. DL 8CAF- 6873 driven by its driver respondent no. 1 Fatehjeet Singh, in a rash and negligent manner, hit their scooter.
Due to this accident, they both fell down on the road.
The car after the accident collided with the divider of the road.
Public persons present nearby apprehended respondent no.1 and also beaten him.
The injured were taken to the hospital for treatment.
Rahul Jain died on the next day on 19.02.2019.

The petitioner suffered grievous injuries in this accident and according to his disability certificate, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 5%
due to fracture tibia/fibula in relation to lower limbs.
3. The respondent no. 3 insurance company - SBI General Insurance Co. Ltd. has taken the general defences and gave a legal offer of Yash Kumar Gupta versus Fatehjeet Singh & others Rs.92,000/-.

sentences.text: On 15.01.2020 this amount was released to the petitioner as interim compensation on the ground that it was the admitted amount of the insurance company.
This order of interim compensation was challenged before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.

On 14.12.2022, the interim award was set aside on the ground that once the legal offer was rejected by the petitioners, they were not entitled for the amount quoted in the legal offer as interim compensation.

4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 19.12.2020 :-
(i) Whether the Petitioner Yash Kumar Gupta suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident happened on 18.02.2019at 12.30 a.m. (midnight), at Mangal Bazar Red light, Vikas Marg, Shakarpur side, Laxmi Nagar, Delhi, within jurisdiction of PS Shakarpur, due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing registration No.
DL8CAF- 6873 being driven by respondent No.1 / Fatehjeet Singh?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?

(OPP) 
5.
In order to establish his claim, petitioner Yash Kumar Gupta has examined himself as PW-1.
But the respondents did not lead any evidence.

7. The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE No.1: Whether the Petitioner Yash Kumar Gupta suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident happened on 18.02.2019at 12.30 a.m. (midnight), at Mangal Bazar Red light,
Vikas Marg, Shakarpur side, Laxmi Nagar, Delhi, within jurisdiction of PS Shakarpur, due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing registration No. DL8CAF6873 being driven by respondent No.1 / Fatehjeet Singh?

(OPP) 
8.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, the Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
9. Now in this case, the petitioner Yash Kumar Gupta is the injured and witness of the accident.

In order to establish petitioners claim, he has examined himself as PW-1 and proved copy of his Aadhar Card Ex. PW1/1, PAN Card Ex.PW1/2, educational documents Ex.PW1/3, medical prescription and treatment record Ex.PW1/4, medical bills Ex.PW1/5, MLC Ex.PW1/6, DAR Ex.PW1/7, letter reference no. F.1/274/DB/DHAS/2018-2019/1279 dated 19.02.2020 by Dr. Yash Kumar Gupta versus Fatehjeet Singh & others Headgeawar Arogya Sansthan, Karkardooma, Delhi Ex.PW1/8,
photographs of injury Mark-A and summary of medical bills Mark-B.

sentences.text: He stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of the respondent no. 1, who was the driver of the car.
He has deposed that in the intervening night of 17/18.02.2019, he and Rahul Jain were going from Vikas Marg towards Mangal Bazar side on their scooter registration No. DL-7SCG-7972.
Rahul Jain was driving this scooter and he was sitting as pillion.

When they were crossing the road from Vikas Marg to Shakarpur at Mangal Bazar red light a car (Honda City) registration No. DL 8CAF- 6873 driven by its driver respondent no. 1 Fatehjeet Singh, in a rash and negligent manner, hit their scooter.
Due to this accident, they both fell down on the road.
The car after the accident collided with the divider of the road.
The injured were taken to the hospital for treatment.
Rahul Jain died on the next day on 19.02.2019.
He received grievous injuries in this case due to comminuted displaced fracture of the distal shaft of tibia and fibula.
He was admitted in Walia Nursing Home, Delhi on 18.2.2019 and discharged on same day but thereafter he was hospitalsed in Max Healthcare, Delhi from 18.2.2019 to 21.02.2019.
His disability was assessed as 5%.

It is his case that he was working as salesman and accountant with Mr. Sumit Gupta, Fashion Max and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month and spent Rs.12,000/- on attendant, Rs.400/- per day on special diet for six months, Rs.20,000/-
on transportation, and Rs.1,50,000/- on medicines and treatment.
10.
The respondent no. 1 & 2 the driver and owner of the offending vehicle have not denied the accident in their reply.

Although, they Yash Kumar Gupta versus Fatehjeet Singh & others have averred about this defence in their reply but have not proved anything in this regard nor led any Yash Kumar Gupta vs Fatehjeet Singh & Others on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77077535/

11. After investigation, the police filed the chargesheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the car.
Filing of chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima faice points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party do not accept such chargesheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that chargesheet is collusive, it can record that chargesheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the chargesheet.

13. Further because the insurance company by filing the legal offer has admitted its liability to pay compensation to the petitioner, the issue of negligence of respondent no. 1 has also otherwise has become redundant.

sentences.text: In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence, it is proved that Yash Kumar Gupta sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 Fateh Jeet Singh, the driver of the offending car.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE No. 3 Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
15. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured , comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the Yash Kumar Gupta versus Fatehjeet Yash Kumar Gupta vs Fatehjeet Singh & Others on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77077535/
4 Singh & others injured.

entities.text: Yash Kumar Gupta versus Fatehjeet Yash Kumar Gupta vs Fatehjeet Singh & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not resulting loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.
Now, in the present case, the injured Yash Gupta has suffered a fracture in his lower limb which caused a medical disability of 5%.
17. Therefore on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows -

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
18.

Petitioner has stated in his evidence affidavit that after his accident, he remained hospitalised in Walia Nursing Home from 18.02.2019 to 21.02.2019 and that he has spent around Rs.15,000/- on his medical treatment.
He has placed on record certain medical bills which are found to be of Rs.91740/- on calculation.
Under this head, actual bills are reimbursed.
Therefore, I award Rs.91,740/- as medical expenses to the petitioner.

Yash Kumar Gupta versus Fatehjeet Singh & others PAIN AND SUFFERING:
19.

entities.text: Yash Kumar Gupta versus Fatehjeet Singh & others PAIN AND SUFFERING
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After the accident, petitioner remained in hospital for around 4 days.
The petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in this case which was fracture of his left lower limb.
As per disability certificate, he suffered a permanent disability to the extent of 5% disability due to this fracture.
The nature of injuries and the disability suffered by him, is a clear proof of the amount of pain and suffering, he must have endured in that accident.

Accordingly, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.25,000/-
to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 20.

The petitioner has claimed Rs.20,000/- for his conveyance and Rs.400/- per day for special diet but he has not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.5,000/- to petitioner for conveyance and special diet charges.
21. Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment and he has not claimed anything under this head.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the Yash Kumar Gupta vs Fatehjeet Singh & Others on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77077535/
5 petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.

sentences.text: 22. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.10,000/- (5,000+5,000) under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :
23.
Petitioner has claimed that he was working as salesman and earning Rs.20,000/- per month but again there is no evidence to this effect.
Accordingly, the notional income of the petitioner is fixed at minimum wages of State of Delhi at the time accident (17/18.02.2019) which were Rs.15,400/- for semi-skilled category.

(Manusha Sreekumar and Others vs United India Insurance Company Ltd.
Civil Appeal No. 7593/2022 dated 17/10/2022-Supreme Court-2022 LiveLaw(SC) 858).

sentences.text:
Therefore,
in that event, petitioner's income is taken as Rs.15,400/-per month.
The discharge slip of hospital shows that the petitioner remained hospitalized for around 4 days.
There is no evidence for how long the petitioner was unable to work.
But it is not difficult to presume that in case of fracture he must have been disabled from work for a least three months as this would have been the minimum time to heel his wound.
Therefore, I award Rs.46,200/- (15,400x3) as compensation under this head.
Therefore, his loss of income for one month is calculated as Rs.46,200/-.
LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO PERMANENT DISABILITY.
24. The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the disability of the petitioner.
Under this head, it has to be seen that what could be the future loss of income on account of disability.

The disability certificate of Dr. Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan Yash Kumar Gupta versus Fatehjeet Singh & others clearly shows that the petitioner is the case of 5% disability due fracture in relation to left lower limb.

entities.text: Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan Yash Kumar Gupta versus Fatehjeet Singh & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though the doctor has been examined but even the petitioner has not narrated how this disability will come in way of reducing the efficiency of the work in which the petitioner is engaged.
But because the petitioner has 5% disability due to fracture in left lower limb, it is not difficult to assume that this disability will affect his day-to-day life and profession.
Therefore, I presume that the petitioner must have suffered at least 2.5% functional disability which is half of 5%, also in carrying on with his profession.
In view of this, I believe that functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner must be considered as 2.5% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.

On the basis of his income taken as Rs.15,400/- per month, the petitioner's annual income shall be Rs.1,84,800/-.
25.

The copy of Aadhar card of the petitioner shows the date of birth of petitioner as 1992, which would mean that he was around 37 years of age at the time of accident and thus, multiplier of 15 would be applicable.

Further, an addition of income of injured for future prospects to the extent of 40% has to be considered as the age of the petitioner was under the age of 40 years (National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Pappu Dev Yadav vs Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online SC 752 and Sohan Lal vs. Taj Khan & Ors., 2019 ACJ Yash Kumar Gupta vs Fatehjeet Singh & Others on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77077535/
6 252, Rajasthan High Court).

In this, yearly income, a multiplier of 15 Yash Kumar Gupta versus Fatehjeet Singh & others will make the future income as 258720x15= Rs.38,80,800/-.

Therefore, this amount is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
LOSS OF AMENITIES 26.
Further, the petitioner is granted Rs.10,000/- for loss of amenities.
